title: Wise vs PayPal: Which Is Better for Receiving International Payments?
summary: Compare Wise vs PayPal for international payments in India. See the real fees, exchange rates, settlement times, FIRA support, and which option saves more.
body_markdown:
## **What Is Wise?**


[Wise](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/infinity-vs-wise) , formerly TransferWise, is a multi-currency payment platform. For me as an Indian professional, it helps in receiving international payments in major currencies like USD, GBP, EUR, SGD, etc. Wise provides me with Wise multi-currency account details, and by using this, my clients can pay me using their domestic payment methods.


Once the money is received in my Wise account, the money is automatically converted into INR using the live exchange rate and settled in my domestic Indian account within 2-5 days.


Wise does not charge any hidden fees in the rate it shows me. This makes Wise a globally trusted brand that offers 100% transparency for me.


## **What is PayPal?**


[PayPal](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/how-to-use-paypal-in-india-2026) is a global wallet, checkout button, and invoicing tool all rolled into one. For Indian professionals, it is available only for international transactions. You cannot use PayPal to make domestic transactions.


PayPal’s global trust, familiarity and convenience make it valuable. Your international client might prefer PayPal over any other payment platform because of the trusted checkout flow, and because of the buyer protection that it offers.


But this convenience comes with a cost. PayPal charges transaction fees, currency conversion fees (depending on the currency), and FX markup as well. Also, with PayPal, you cannot hold your international payment, and it will be automatically converted into INR. The final amount is settled to your Indian bank account within 7 days. PayPal's real strength shows up on the e-commerce and marketplace side, not on straightforward freelance or B2B invoicing.


## **Wise vs PayPal Fees in India**


Let's take an example of $1000, using an illustrative rate of ₹94 per USD.


### **Wise:**


-


Gross amount: $1,000


-


Conversion fee (around 1.65%): $16.50


-


GST (18% on the fee): $2.97


-


FIRA certificate: $2


-


Net USD after fees: approximately $978


-


Estimated INR received: approximately ₹91,900


### **PayPal:**


-


Gross amount: $1,000


-


Transaction fee (4.4%): $44


-


Fixed fee: $0.30


-


GST (18% on the fee): $7.97


-


Net USD before FX conversion: approximately $948


-


FX markup (around 3.5%): reduces the effective rate from ₹94 to roughly ₹90.70


-


Estimated INR received: approximately ₹86,000


On a $1000 invoice, there is a difference of 5,900 in Wise's favour. This difference looks small on one invoice, but the amounts get compounded over the year, and the difference keeps increasing.


## **Exchange Rate: Why the Final INR Amount Changes**


This is an important part that you might miss, and it is usually the highest cost in an international transaction.


There is a difference between the transaction fee, which is disclosed upfront, and the FX spread, which is hidden in the conversion fees and not disclosed upfront (not always).


Wise uses the mid-market rate, the same one you would see on Google or Reuters. What you receive is close to what you see on screen before confirming a transfer. PayPal does the opposite.


PayPal applies its own conversion fees, FX markup, and a transaction fee. You do not see "FX markup: 3.5%" anywhere on the transaction; you just see a lower amount landing in your account than expected.


This is why two platforms with seemingly similar headline costs can produce very different real payouts.


## **Settlement Time: How Fast Do You Get Paid in India?**


Wise typically settles within 2-5 days for most major currencies. However, the first transaction might take some time because Wise might ask for some additional details like the sender’s details or the purpose of the payment as a regulatory check.


[PayPal's settlement](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/paypal-funds-on-hold) is less predictable. The standard settlement time for Indian professionals is around 5-7 days. However, newer accounts and larger payments that might fail PayPal’s risk check can take about 7-14 days.


This is the pattern behind most of the "PayPal held my payment" complaints you will find from Indian freelancers. It is not always a rule violation; it is often just PayPal's own review process on unfamiliar or high-value transactions.


## **FIRA, FIRC, GST, and RBI Compliance**


If you are an Indian freelancer, agency, or exporter, this section matters more than the fee comparison.[FIRA (Foreign Inward Remittance Advice)](https://www.infinityapp.in/fira-analyzer) is proof that you have received an international payment through a legitimate banking channel. You will need FIRA for GST refunds on zero-rated exports, for accounting purposes, for FEMA compliance, and for your bank’s own reconciliation.


Wise offers you FIRA for $2 per certificate. FIRA is a reliable document that is important while receiving international payments. But paying $2.50 every time you receive an international payment can add up to a larger amount.


PayPal also offers FIRA that is free of charge. But it provides a weekly FIRA instead of a FIRA per transaction.


Regardless of which platform you use, you must keep your FIRA and other documents ready as proof of payment.


## **Which Is Better for Freelancers in India?**


**A new direct client:** For a $1,000 payment, Wise gives around ₹85,000 after fees. PayPal gives around ₹79,000-80,000 due to higher fees and a hidden FX markup. That's about ₹5,000-6,000 lost with PayPal, plus a possible hold since it's a new client relationship.


**A recurring retainer client:** This is where Infinity really helps. For a $2,000 monthly retainer, Wise charges 1% plus GST and USD 2 for every FIRA certificate, so the FIRA cost alone adds up to $24 a year. Infinity charges a flat 0.5% and gives the FIRA instantly, free. Over a year, that's about ₹12,000+ saved compared to Wise.


**A one-off small project:** If a client insists on PayPal for something small, like $200, it's usually fine to go with it. The loss is small (₹800-1,000) and not worth losing the client over.


**A high-ticket invoice:** This is where PayPal hurts the most. On a $10,000 invoice, PayPal's fees and FX markup can cost $600-700 (₹51,000-60,000). Infinity's flat 0.5% fee costs only $50 (₹4,300). That's almost ₹50,000 saved on one invoice alone.


**Bottom line:** Depending on invoice size and frequency, Infinity can save anywhere from ₹15,000 to ₹60,000+ a year compared to PayPal. Infinity still beats Wise once FIRA charges and GST are added.

## **Which Is Better for Agencies, Exporters, and SaaS Businesses?**


Once you move past occasional freelance payments into repeat invoicing, reconciliation and purpose codes start to matter as much as the fee itself. Agencies that invoice multiple clients need FIRA documentation that is easy to match against specific invoices for accounting purposes.


Wise's flat fee per-certificate and PayPal's weekly bundled FIRA work, but neither was built for high-frequency B2B invoicing as the primary use case.


This is where a platform like Infinity helps. Infinity is built specifically around AD-1 bank and RBI PA-CB compliance for Indian exporters, freelancers and startup founders to reduce friction. Infinity also provides free and instant FIRA.


This helps your finance team to reconcile against invoices immediately rather than waiting for a weekly batch or paying per certificate. At scale, this saves real time even before you account for the fee difference.


## **Which Is Better for E-commerce and Digital Products?**


This is genuinely PayPal's strongest ground, and it deserves a fair hearing. If you are selling digital products, subscriptions, or running an online store where international customers expect to see a PayPal checkout button, PayPal's familiarity and buyer protection does help a lot to the clients. Wise, on the other side, was not built for checkout process at all.


However, this familiarity comes with a cost. PayPal charges a 4.4% plus fixed fee plus FX markup structure. Many e-commerce sellers keep PayPal as a checkout option specifically because customers expect it..


## **Final Recommendation**


**Choose Wise if** you're comfortable with bank transfers and your main priority is keeping your FX costs visible, with no hidden markups.


**Choose PayPal if** your overseas client already uses PayPal, refuses bank transfers, or you want the comfort of PayPal's dispute and buyer protection system.


**Choose**[Infinity](https://www.infinityapp.in/) **if** you want the lower fees of Wise along with faster settlement, free instant FIRA, and RBI-regulated compliance. Infinity is definitely worth comparing with Wise and PayPal before you decide.
